description: The bar chart illustrates the Shapley values for three different models—mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (light green)—across various linguistic feature categories labeled along the x-axis as L₄⁺, L₃, L₂, L₁, T, R₁, R₂, R₃, and R₄⁺, which likely represent different layers or types of morphosyntactic features in the context of probing multilingual BERT models. The y-axis, labeled “Shapley value,” ranges from 0 to 80 with tick marks at intervals of 20, indicating the relative contribution of each model to the prediction for each feature category. The tallest bar corresponds to the chLSTM model on category T, reaching approximately 80, followed closely by mBERT and XLM-R on the same category at around 60 and 55 respectively. For most other categories, the Shapley values are substantially lower, with many near or below 10; for instance, L₄⁺ shows values around 5–6 for mBERT and XLM-R, while chLSTM is near zero. The R₃ and R₄⁺ categories show minimal contributions across all models, with bars barely rising above the baseline. The chart uses grouped bars for each category, allowing direct comparison between models, and the legend in the upper right corner clearly identifies each model by color. The overall pattern suggests that the T category is most influential for all models, especially for chLSTM, while the right-side categories (R₁–R₄⁺) contribute minimally.
